fields.why: 52 cases described by proportions; the Table and Figure split them by known vs unknown exposure side by side, but the text draws no contrast. 'limited' (descriptive case series) is the closer reading; 'yes' is defensible because v5 counts a side-by-side split as comparison.
Follows data_focus: summary only if the known/unknown split is a descriptive breakdown; adding comparison is defensible from the side-by-side Table columns.
No claim rests on known vs unknown exposure; 'pair' is defensible only if the side-by-side Table/Figure columns are read as a comparison (scale null).

No design named; a descriptive series of 52 surveillance-reported cases with desk review and reinterview. Adding surveillance/descriptive is defensible; the article also calls itself an 'investigation' within the outbreak response.

Gender identity (cisgender man/woman, transgender woman) is a composite variable: v5 records SOGI plus its sex component, and MMSC itself is defined on sex. B's sex basis should be 'assigned or observed', not self-identified.

brief_issues: Brief does not say whether a case series' side-by-side split by a non-SPD classifier (known vs unknown exposure) with no text contrast is 'comparison'; a rule that the split must carry a claim would decide it.
